brand.name.hint: The company name shown in the rail, the sign-in page and the title. Shared with the landing.

brand.tagline.hint: One line that says what you do and for whom. Shared with the landing.

brand.color.hint: Any CSS color: hex, rgb(), hsl(), oklch(), oklab(), lab(), lch(), color(srgb ...) or color(display-p3 ...). Shared with the landing; it becomes the accent, the rest stays warm neutral, and every pair is checked for AA contrast.

brand.format.hint: How the generated tokens are written in CSS. Shared with the landing.

link.email.hint: Shown on the sign-in page and in the disclaimer. Shared with the landing.

link.landing.hint: The full address of the public landing page. Running both on this computer: http://localhost:4321.

assistant.name.hint: What the assistant is called in the chat, one or two words.

assistant.role.hint: The system prompt: who it helps, what it does with voice and photos, what it must never do, and when it sends people to a professional or emergency services. At least 80 characters.

assistant.greeting.hint: Shown above the composer and on the sign-in page. Wrap the second half in *stars* to set it in the lighter grey.

assistant.intro.hint: One sentence under the headline that says what people can ask, say or show.

assistant.disclaimer.hint: Shown under the composer on every chat: what the assistant is not, and where to go in an emergency.

starter.1.hint: A first message people can tap, written the way your user would say it.

starter.2.hint: A first message people can tap, written the way your user would say it.

starter.3.hint: A first message people can tap, written the way your user would say it.

onboard.title.hint: The first thing people read when they open the app, four to eight words. Wrap the second half in *stars* to set it in the lighter grey.

onboard.body.hint: One or two sentences on what the next few questions are for and how they help.

onboard.start.hint: Two to four words on the button that starts the questions.

onboard.name.hint: The question that asks what to call the person, as the assistant would ask it.

onboard.1.question.hint: A question with one answer that tells the assistant who it is helping, such as the person's role.

onboard.1.options.hint: Three to five answers, separated by commas.

onboard.2.question.hint: A question people can answer with several picks, such as what they want help with.

onboard.2.options.hint: Three to six answers, separated by commas.

onboard.3.question.hint: A last question with one answer, such as how they like to talk to the assistant.

onboard.3.options.hint: Three to five answers, separated by commas.

onboard.done.hint: Four to eight words shown above the safety line and the final button. Wrap the second half in *stars* to set it in the lighter grey.

onboard.cta.hint: Two to four words on the button that opens the app.

env.base.hint: An OpenAI-compatible API base, ending in /v1 (OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, Together, DeepInfra, Fireworks or your own). Saved to .env, never committed.

env.key.hint: The key for that API. Saved to .env, never committed.

env.model.hint: A chat model id on that API that also reads images, for photos and handwriting.

env.transcribe.hint: A speech-to-text model id on that API for the microphone (served at /audio/transcriptions).
